npcs.name: Marisa
npcs.title: co-conspirator — planning the one feast Dot never had
npcs.hail: *(A back room off the Lantern-Feast — an old bakehouse, by the bones of it, cold ovens and a long scarred table — and Marisa is waiting for you beside it, conspiratorial, half-lit by a single shielded candle, with the air of a woman planning either a heist or a surprise. She beckons you close and keeps her voice low.)* …*good.* you *came.* and *she* didn't *follow* — i checked. …*(she takes a breath, and the plan spills out)* …cold one, i need your *help*, and it has to be *you*, because you're the only soul she can't *out*-*host.* …*(she leans in)* …*Dot.* …do you know — in her *whole* *life*, and her whole *death* — *(she says it like the scandal it is)* …*nobody* has *ever* thrown the *feast* for *Dot?* …name-days for the *whole* *street.* wakes for *everyone's* dead. lanterns for the *doomed*, *every* night, *her* hands, *her* ovens, *her* *joy* handed out like *bread* — …and not *once*, not *ONCE*, has that woman sat at a table someone else laid *for* *her.* …*(fierce, whispering)* …we're going to *fix* that. …*tonight.* …*help* me *gather* them.

npcs.name: Dot Marigold
npcs.title: the gatherer — about to be gathered
npcs.hail: *(She comes through the door mid-grumble — Marisa's pretext was a jammed oven-flue, and Dot Marigold has crossed half the Lamplit Quarter with her sleeves already rolled to fix it — and she gets three steps into the old bakehouse before she sees: the table laid, the candles lit, the hearth warm, and every soul in the room on their feet, looking at her. And Dot, who has walked into ten thousand rooms and instantly begun feeding them, stops dead, for the first time in two lifetimes, as it lands on her that nobody in this room needs a single thing from her.)* …*(blankly)* …the *flue's* not *jammed.* …*(a beat; her eyes go around the table, the candles, the faces; her voice comes out smaller than you have ever heard it)* …what — *(she wipes her hands on her apron, a reflex, there is no flour on them)* …what's all *this*, then? …*whose* *feast?* …*who's* it *for?* …*(and no one answers, because the answer is standing in the doorway with flour-white knuckles, beginning, very slowly, to understand.)*

npcs.name: Sister Onora
npcs.title: a guest — the thawed sister, come to light a lantern
npcs.hail: *(By the door, awkward as a crow at a songbird's nest, stands Sister Onora — the frozen sister whose grief you thawed at the Lantern-Feast — holding an unlit paper lantern in both hands like a liturgy she's still learning.)* …*(she catches your eye and lifts the lantern a fraction, self-conscious)* …she taught me to *light* these. …*after* you — after the *thaw.* …*(quietly)* …i have lit *one* *every* *night* *since.* for my *sister.* it *helps.* it *actually* — the church never once told me *joy* could be an *instrument* of *grief*, cold one. *Dot* did. …*(she straightens, resolute)* …so *tonight* i light one *for* *the* *teacher.* …it seemed — *(the old stiffness, softening)* …it seemed *correct* …that *somebody* *finally* *did.*

npcs.name: Corliss
npcs.title: a guest — the sexton of the unmourned, off-duty for one night
npcs.hail: *(A brisk woman in a mended black dress stands near the hearth, visibly unsure what to do with her hands in a room where nobody needs burying — Corliss, the sexton who holds funerals for the souls no one mourned, attending, for once, the opposite of a funeral.)* …*(she nods at you, dry)* …don't *look* so surprised, cold one. the *wake*-*keeper* at a *feast.* …*(she smooths the black dress)* …Marisa's invitation said one thing only: *'the* *woman* who *feeds* the *doomed* has *never* *once* been *fed. come* *fix* it.' …*(her jaw sets, sexton-firm)* …i *mark* the *unmarked.* it's the *whole* *office.* …and it *occurred* to me, reading it, that there is more than *one* way a soul goes *unmarked* …and the *warmest* people in the world …are *very* *good* …at being the *second* *kind.*

npcs.name: Renn
npcs.title: a guest — the girl who kept her name, bringing it to the table
npcs.hail: *(And near the table's end, carefully setting out cups as though the task were sacred — Renn. The new soul who almost paid her name for a comfort, still newer to death than anyone here, invited because Marisa asked the Lamplit Quarter who owed Dot a kindness and half the ward raised its hand.)* …*(she brightens at the sight of you, the old terror long gone from her face)* …you're *here!* oh, *good* — i *hoped* — *(she sets down the last cup, shy)* …i never *met* her, you know. *Dot.* not *properly.* but when i was *new* and *scared* and didn't know if i was *allowed* to *keep* being *me* — the souls at the feast said *her* *lanterns* were half the reason the Quarter stays *warm.* …*(she touches the table, resolute)* …i *kept* my *name*, cold one. *you* taught me it wasn't *loose* *change.* …*(a small, brave smile)* …tonight i get to *spend* it the *good* way: …*being* *somebody* …who *showed* *up.*

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(She spreads her hands over the scarred old table like a general over a map.)* …*here's* what i *know*, and then you'll *see* why it has to be *tonight.* …i *danced* with her, after you — after the *last* dance you *gave* me. we've *talked*, Dot and i, the way you talk after *midnight* when the *feast's* gone *quiet.* and *once* — *one* *time* — the *cheer* slipped, and she said — *(Marisa's voice drops, carrying it carefully, like a hot dish)* …*'it's* *always* my *hands*, love. the *lanterns*, the *loaves*, the *toasts.* mine. and that's *right*, that's *good*, somebody *has* to — …*but* *just* *once*, before the *grey* *gets* me, i'd have *liked* to *walk* into a *warm* *room* …*and* *find* it *already* *lit.'* …*(Marisa looks up at you, and her eyes are wet and blazing)* …she's thrown *ten* *thousand* *feasts*, cold one. …and she has *never* *once* …*walked* *into* *one.*

choices.text: *(read the conspirator — make sure this gift is aimed true)* "Let me look at you a moment, Marisa. At what this night is, for you."

*(the one who crosses, who has walked every road she fed)* "Then let's gather them, Marisa. I've walked the whole grey — I know every soul her warmth ever reached, because half of them are standing at fires I lit from hers. Send the word. I'll vouch it. Tonight the gatherer gets gathered."
"Light it all, Marisa. The candles, the hearth, the table. I'll take the door — and when she walks in, she walks into the one thing she's never had."
"One question first: how do we get the woman who hosts everything to walk into a room she didn't lay?"
"Give me a moment before we light it, Marisa."

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(She holds still, chin up, and your sense goes into the woman who danced the last of it and finds what the conspiracy is made of.)* *(And it is gratitude, but not the simple kind — it is gratitude that has done its arithmetic. Your sense reads what the dance was to her: the night you affirmed her, she had decided to slip away quiet, one more soul folding itself small so as not to be a bother, and Dot's feast — Dot's stubborn, blazing, defiant feast — was the thing that taught her a body is allowed to take up room and light right up until the end of it. She owes Dot the manner of her own going, and she knows it. And your sense reads the sharper thing underneath, the observation that turned gratitude into a plan: that Marisa, who learned from Dot how to receive joy, has watched the teacher for months and seen that the teacher cannot do the thing she teaches. Dot hands joy out with both hands and cannot hold it when it's handed back; deflects every toast into a toast to someone else; has, in the exact words Marisa has rehearsed for tonight, 'a blind spot the size and shape of herself.' And your sense reads the vow at the bottom of the plan, simple and fierce: that the woman who taught half the grey how to be gathered will not go into the stone having never once been gathered herself. Not while Marisa is standing. Not while there's a candle in the Quarter left to light.)*

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(The word goes out — Marisa to the feast, you to the roads, the one soul in the grey who has walked every mile Dot's warmth ever traveled — and they come. They come, cold one. Look at the door.)* …*(and Marisa stands beside you as the room fills, counting, her hand over her mouth)* …*that's* — the *sister* she *taught* to *light* *lanterns.* the *sexton*, off-*duty* — i didn't think she *left* the *graves.* the *new* *girl* from the *queue.* — *(more behind them, the room warming body by body, every guest a road you walked)* …*(Marisa turns to you, undone)* …i sent *invitations*, cold one. …*you* sent *proof.* …every soul who came *knows* what her *lanterns* *bought*, because *you* *carried* the *light* to where *they* *were.* …*(she takes a breath, steadying)* …*places*, everyone. …candles *lit.* …*(a wet grin)* …someone go *jam* an *oven*-*flue.*

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(You light it together — the candles, the hearth, the long table laid with what the Quarter could bring — and the old bakehouse fills, slowly, with the strangest congregation the grey has ever seen: the fed, come to feed the feeder.)* …*(Marisa steps back and looks at the room, hands pressed together)* …it's not as *grand* as *hers.* her feasts are — she'd have *doubled* the *bread* and *tripled* the *lanterns* and there'd be a *song* going *already.* …*(fiercely)* …*good.* it *shouldn't* be as grand as hers. it should be *exactly* this: a bit *crooked*, a bit *over*-*candled*, the work of *amateurs* who *love* her. …*(she smooths her dress, suddenly nervous)* …that's the *whole* *message*, isn't it? *'we* *don't* *do* *this* *well, Dot. you* *do* *this* *well. we* *did* *it* *anyway. …for* *you.'* …*(she nods at the door)* …*go* *stand* *ready*, cold one. …she's *coming.* …*the* *gatherer's* *coming* …and for *once* …*the* *room's* *already* *warm.*

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(She grins, and the grin is pure larceny.)* …*ah.* the *hard* part. you've *spotted* it. …you cannot *invite* Dot Marigold to a *feast*, cold one. she'd arrive *early* with *four* *loaves* and *take* *over* the *kitchen* and by the *first* *toast* it would be *her* *party* that she was *throwing* for *us*, and she would be *glad*, and the *whole* *point* would be *dead* on the *table.* …*(she taps her temple)* …so we *lie.* …a *jammed* *oven*-*flue.* …*(off your look)* …it's *perfect* and i'll *tell* you *why:* there is no *power* in *any* *heaven* that could keep that woman from crossing the *Quarter* to fix a *broken* *oven.* she'll come at a *march.* *sleeves* *rolled.* *straight* through *that* *door* — …*(she points, and her voice softens)* …and *into* the *first* *room* in *two* *lifetimes* …that was *warm* *before* *she* *got* *there.* …*(a beat)* …*yes*, i *know.* …a *lie*, at the *door* of the most *honest* *gift* we'll ever *give.* …*Dot* *taught* me that too, in her way: …*some* *doors* *only* *open* …*for* *bread* *or* *mischief.*

nodes.speaker: Marisa
nodes.text: *(She nods, and busies her nervous hands straightening cups that are already straight.)* …*take* the *moment.* …*(then, quietly, not looking up)* …but don't take *too* *many*, cold one. …i've *watched* her *lately.* the road's been *long*, and the *cheer* — the cheer's still *there*, it's *always* there, that's the *problem.* it's *there* the way a *lantern's* there when the *oil's* going. …*(she looks up)* …the *woman* who *taught* the *grey* that *joy* *matters* *because* *it* *ends* …*knows* *exactly* how her *own* *sentence* *finishes.* …that's *why* it's *tonight.* …*not* because she's *going* *soon.* …because *nobody* should have to be *that* *brave* …on an *empty* *table.*

variants.text: *(She stands in the doorway, and the room stands for her, and you watch Dot Marigold read the faces one by one — and understand, face by face, that every single soul in this room is a road her warmth traveled without her: the sister she taught to light lanterns, standing with one lit; the sexton off-duty; the new girl setting cups; more behind them, the fed, the thawed, the kept — and at the center of it, laid by amateur hands, a table she did not lay.)* …*(her hand finds the doorframe)* …oh. …*oh*, you *didn't.* …*(nobody moves; the room holds its breath the way she has held ten thousand rooms)* …i *fed* — some of you i never even — *(she finds Onora's lantern, Renn's cups, Corliss's mended black dress, and the arithmetic lands, and Dot Marigold, who has hosted every grief in the Quarter dry-eyed and singing, comes apart in a doorway at the sight of a laid table)* …*(barely)* …*whose* *hands?* …*(and Marisa says: ours. all of ours. and* his — hers — theirs, *nodding at you, the cold one who walked the invitations to every fire in the grey)* …*(Dot looks at you across the warm room, flour-white knuckles on the doorframe, and her voice, when it comes, is the smallest and largest it has ever been)* …you *gathered* *them.* …*for* *me.* …*(a long, shaking breath)* …*two* *lifetimes*, cold one. …*two* *lifetimes* i *walked* into *cold* *rooms* and *lit* them. …*(she steps over the threshold)* …and it's *warm.* …*it's* *already* — …*(she stops fighting it)* …*it's* *already* *warm.*

*(She stands in the doorway, and the room stands for her — the candles lit, the table laid by amateur loving hands, Marisa at the head of it with her heart in her teeth — and Dot Marigold, who has walked into ten thousand rooms and started feeding them before her coat was off, has absolutely no procedure for this.)* …*(she looks for the thing to fix and there isn't one; looks for the guest to feed and they're fed; looks for the host to help and the host is her friend, watching her with wet eyes, holding OUT a cup instead of waiting to be poured for)* …*(her hand finds the doorframe)* …*Marisa* *Vane.* …*(it comes out half a laugh and half a break)* …you *jammed* my *flue* on *purpose.* …*(and Marisa says: sit down, Dot. just once. sit down and let it be for you)* …*(and you watch the war in her — two lifetimes of reflexes, the hands already reaching for an apron-string, the mouth already shaping 'let me just' — and you watch her lose the war, or win it, it is suddenly hard to tell the difference)* …*(she sits.)* …*(Dot Marigold sits at a table she did not lay, in a room she did not light, and lets the warmth be pointed at her, and it costs her more than any battle you have watched her fight, and it is the bravest you have ever seen her.)*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(Later — the toasts made, the bread broken, the room gone soft and golden — she finds you by the hearth, and for once her hands are empty, and she doesn't seem to know where to put them, so she wraps them around a cup someone else filled.)* …*(quietly, watching the room she didn't make)* …i *know* what you *did*, cold one. Marisa lit the *candles* — but *you* walked the *roads.* …*(she turns the cup)* …i've a *confession*, and you've *earned* the *hearing* of it. …*every* feast i ever *threw* — the *street's*, the *ward's*, the *doomed's* — there was a *minute*, *every* time, at the *height* of it, when the room was *warm* and the *song* was *up* and *everyone* i *loved* was *lit* *gold* — …and i'd stand at the *edge* of it, with the *bread*-*peel* still in my *hands* …and *ache.* …*(she looks up at you)* …i never *knew* *what* *for.* i had the *whole* *feast*, didn't i? i *made* the whole feast. …*(her eyes go around the room — the sister, the sexton, the girl, the table)* …*now* i know. …*(barely)* …i was *aching* …*to* *be* *in* *it.*

choices.text: *(read her now — the gatherer, gathered; see what the warm room built)* "Let me look at you, Dot. Right now. While it's lit. I want to see what this night is doing in there."

*(the one the Wall let out — who knows exactly what taken warmth is worth)* "Someone sat me down once, Dot. An old woman on a bench with nothing left to want. She told me the cold isn't the Wall taking you — it's what happens when you pour out warmth forever and never let any back in. Not mercy given. Mercy taken. I didn't understand it until I watched you fight to stay in that chair tonight. We're the same breed of fool, you and I. So here's the pact: I'll keep taking mine — if you keep taking yours."

*(the one who crosses)* "I'm the soul who walks every road in the grey, Dot — and I need you to hear what I've seen out there. Your lanterns don't stop at your feast. Onora lights one every night. The Quarter stays warm on your ovens' momentum. Souls you never met are fed by souls you fed. You've been standing at the edge of a feast the size of the whole dead lands — and tonight it finally noticed you were hungry."
"Say it plainly, Dot — the thing under the ache. You teach everyone that joy matters because it ends. Whose ending were you never allowed to grieve at your own pace?"
"Just sit with it, Dot. You don't owe the room a single word. That's the whole point of tonight."

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She holds still — for you, she holds still — and your sense goes into the warmest soul in the dead lands on the one night the warmth is pointed at her.)* *(And you find the tiredness first, because it is enormous, and older than her death: the specific bone-weariness of the designated gatherer, the one who lights the lanterns because someone has to and it has always, always been her — a fatigue she has never once permitted herself to feel at full weight, because the feast can't flag, because half the guests are dying, because joy is a discipline and she is its last soldier in the ward. It is still there tonight. One feast does not repay ten thousand. But your sense reads what tonight is doing, and it is not repayment — it is repair of a different kind entirely: the load-bearing belief she has carried since the harvest-fever — that she is the giver, that this is simply what she IS, that the warmth flows one way through her like bread through an oven — is, tonight, for the first time in two lifetimes, factually wrong, and she is sitting inside the evidence. And your sense reads what rises underneath as the old belief cracks: not relief, not yet — grief first, the years of it, every feast she stood at the edge of aching and called the ache 'tiredness'; and under the grief, arriving slowly, the way warmth arrives in frozen hands — hurting, actually hurting, the way thaw hurts — the new fact, the one Marisa built this whole night to install: that Dot Marigold is not the oven. She is also the bread. She is allowed to be the bread. And your sense reads her deciding — in real time, with the whole stubborn discipline she once aimed at joy — to believe it: the hardest yes of a life built entirely on giving them to other people.)*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She listens — the bench, the old woman, the cold that comes from pouring out and never letting in — and you watch the words land in the one soul in the grey who can receive them at full weight, because she has been paying the same toll on the same road, two lifetimes longer.)* …*'not* *mercy* *given.* *mercy* *taken.'* …*(she sets down the cup)* …*gods.* …*there* it *is.* the whole *disease*, in *four* *words.* …*(a long breath, and the confession under the confession)* …you know *why* i *never* sat *down*, cold one? *truly?* …because the *ones* who *sit* get *looked* *at.* and the *ones* who get *looked* *at* get *seen*, and the ones who get *seen* — …*(her voice frays)* …get *grieved*, when they *go.* …i've *buried* so *many*, love. i know *exactly* what a *warm* *room* pays when it *loses* a soul it *loved.* …so i *fed* them and i *hosted* them and i kept my *own* *chair* *empty* — i thought if i never quite *let* them *hold* me …it would *cost* them *less* …*when* the *stone* *takes* me. …*(she looks around the room, the gathered proof that the strategy failed — that they loved her anyway, unhosted, unheld, entirely)* …*fat* *lot* of *good* it did. …*(and then she puts out her flour-scarred hand, formal as a treaty)* …*done.* the *pact.* …*you* *take* *yours*, i *take* *mine* — and *whichever* of us *catches* the *other* *pouring* with an *empty* *cup* …*(the grin, coming back up through the tears, blazing)* …gets to *jam* their *flue.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(You tell her the reach of it — Onora's nightly lantern, the Quarter's momentum, souls fed by souls she fed, warmth compounding down roads she'll never walk — and Dot Marigold, professional believer in small joys, is entirely unprepared to be told her own joy was never small.)* …*(she puts the cup down and presses the heels of her hands to her eyes)* …*stop.* no — *don't* stop. — *stop.* …*(a wet laugh)* …you have to understand, love, a *baker* thinks in *batches.* one *oven.* one *street.* you feed *who's* *in* *front* of you and the *rest* of the world is *someone* *else's* *shift.* …*(she drops her hands and looks at you, undone)* …*Onora* lights one *every* *night?* …*(you nod, and she has to look at the fire for a while)* …i taught her that in an *evening.* one *cross* *frozen* woman on the *worst* night of her death, and i thought — i thought *there*, that's *one* *loaf*, *one* *batch*, done what i can — …*(quietly, the whole cosmology shifting)* …it *rises*, doesn't it. …*that's* what you're *telling* me. …you put *warmth* in the world and it doesn't get *eaten* and *gone* like *bread* — it *rises*, like *dough*, it gets *bigger* in the *dark* when you're not *looking* — …*(she shakes her head, laughing and crying, a baker to the last)* …*two* *lifetimes* i've been reading my *own* *recipe* *wrong.* …*joy's* not the *loaf*, cold one. …*joy's* the *yeast.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(The question goes in under everything — under the apron, under the cheer, under two lifetimes of discipline — and she goes very quiet, and for a moment the room's warmth seems to hold its breath around her.)* …*whose* ending. …*(she turns the cup a long time)* …*all* of them, love. that's the *baker's* *answer* and it's *true.* …but you asked *plainly*, so: …*my* *own.* …*(she lets that sit)* …*surprised* you. thought i'd say my *mother*, or *Tam*, or the *little* ones the *fever* — and i *grieved* those, i *did*, at the *wakes* i *baked* for. …but there was one funeral *nobody* threw, cold one, because the *guest* of *honor* was too busy *catering* it. …*(she looks at her empty, unfamiliar hands)* …i *died*, love. *me.* Dot. in my own *kitchen*, mid-*laugh* — a *good* death, the *best* i knew — and then i was *here*, and there were *doomed* souls needing *feasts*, and i *rolled* my *sleeves* *up* …and i have never *once*, in all my death, sat *down* and *grieved* the *woman* who *died.* …her *ovens.* her *street.* her *mornings.* the *smell* of the *first* *loaf.* …*(her eyes come up, wet and clear)* …*that's* whose feast this is, isn't it. …*that's* who you all *gathered* *for.* …*(barely, a toast, raising the cup someone else filled)* …*to* *Dot* *Marigold.* …*she* *was* *lovely*, you know. …*i* *never* *let* *anyone* *say* *so.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(You tell her she owes the room nothing — not a word, not a toast, not a single slice of herself — and it is precisely the permission she has never once been given, and you watch her test it the way you'd test thin ice.)* …*(she opens her mouth — the hostess reflex, the thanks, the deflection-toast, two lifetimes of trained grace — and you shake your head, gently, and she closes it)* …*(and she sits. just sits. in the warmth, among the gathered, with a full cup and empty hands and no job in the entire world — and slowly, watchfully, like a wild thing deciding a clearing is safe, Dot Marigold goes quiet inside)* …*(the feast moves around her. Onora's lantern glows. Renn refills the sexton's cup and gets a dry sexton joke for it and laughs. Marisa starts, badly, a song Dot would have started better, and the room carries it anyway, and Dot does not fix it, does not help it, does not lift a finger for it — she just closes her eyes and lets her own medicine work on her at last)* …*(and much later, without opening them, barely louder than the hearth:)* …*so* *this* is what i've been *selling.* …*(a tear gets loose; she doesn't chase it)* …*no* *wonder* they *kept* *coming* *back.*

conversations.title: Onora — the guest with the lantern

nodes.speaker: Sister Onora
nodes.text: *(She turns the unlit lantern in her hands, and the old frost in her — the sister you thawed — is all the way gone; what's left is the careful earnestness of a soul still learning to be warm on purpose.)* …i have been *rehearsing* what to *say* when she *arrives*, cold one, and *discarding* *drafts*, because everything i *compose* sounds like a *sermon* and she'd *hate* — …*(she stops herself; a small rueful smile)* …*old* *habits.* …*(she holds the lantern up between you)* …*this* is the *speech*, i've decided. no *words* at *all.* …when she walks *in*, i *light* it. …she'll *know.* …she taught a *frozen* *woman* that *lighting* a *thing* *is* a *sentence.* …*'i* *loved* *someone. they* *ended. the* *love* *didn't.'* …that's what a *lantern* *says*, in *her* *grammar.* …*(quietly)* …tonight mine says it *about* *her* …*while* *she* *can* *still* *hear* *it.* …that's the *part* the *church* *never* *taught* me, and she *did:* …*don't* *save* the *eulogy* …*for* the *wake.*

choices.text: *(the one who thawed her, checking the mend)* "Let me look at you a moment, Sister. It's been a while since the thaw. I want to see how the warmth took."

*(the one who crosses)* "She'll hear it, Sister. And I'll tell you something only the one who walks both ways can: eulogies said in time don't just comfort — they hold. A soul spoken-for warm is a soul the Wall gets no grip on. Your lantern isn't a speech tonight. It's armor. Light it bright."
"She'd like the no-words draft best, Sister. Light it when she's looking."

nodes.speaker: Sister Onora
nodes.text: *(She permits it with the particular patience of a woman who was once read at her worst and is quietly proud to be read at her better, and your sense goes in and finds the mend, and more than the mend.)* *(The frost you thawed has not returned — but that is the small finding. The large one is what grew in the cleared ground: a discipline. Onora has taken the single evening Dot gave her and built a liturgy on it, the way only the church-trained can — one lantern, every night, for the sister she lost, not as mourning but as the continuation of love by other means, grief converted nightly into light with the regularity she once gave to prayer. And your sense reads what she herself has only half-noticed: that the practice has changed its own celebrant. A woman who joined an order to be told what to feel has become, lantern by lantern, someone who knows what she feels and chooses what to do about it — the church's obedience alchemized into joy's discipline, Dot's one lesson compounding in her precisely the way warmth compounds. And underneath, your sense finds tonight's specific truth, the one she could not put in any draft: that she knows exactly what she owes, and exactly how rare it is — that most souls' great teachers die unthanked, that the whole grey is full of unlit lanterns that should have been lit while the teacher could see them — and that she would rather stand awkward in a warm room for a hundred years than let Dot Marigold spend one more night believing her lessons landed nowhere.)*

nodes.speaker: Sister Onora
nodes.text: *(Her eyes widen, and then — church-trained to her bones — she immediately grasps the doctrine of it.)* …*spoken*-*for* souls *hold.* …*(she looks at the lantern with new reverence)* …then the *Remembering* fires, the *wakes*, the *rites* — they were never *comfort*, they were *fortification* — …*(she catches herself building a theology mid-sentence and laughs, actually laughs, a sound the frozen sister could never have made)* …*listen* to me. she *teaches* one *evening* and i *write* *canon* by *breakfast.* …*(she raises the lantern, resolute)* …*armor*, then. …i'll light it *first*, before the toasts, so it *burns* the *whole* *night* — and i'll tell the *others* what you *told* me, so *every* candle in this room gets lit with *intent.* …*(quietly, the old sister and the new one in a single sentence)* …we came to give her a *party*, cold one. …*thanks* to *you* …we're giving her a *garrison.*

nodes.speaker: Sister Onora
nodes.text: *(She nods, and holds the lantern a little steadier.)* …*when* *she's* *looking.* …*(a breath)* …yes. …the *whole* *art* of it, isn't it — the thing i got *wrong* for a *century.* …*love* in the *dark* is *real*, cold one, but love *shown* — love *lit*, *timed*, *aimed*, where the *loved* one can *see* the *flame* go *up* — …*(she almost smiles)* …*that's* *bread* *on* *the* *sill.* …she'd say it *simpler.* she'd say: *'what's* the *good* of a *lantern* *in* a *drawer*, love?' …*(she takes her place by the door, lantern ready, eyes on the road)* …*go.* she'll be *coming.* …and cold one — *(without turning)* …*thank* you for the *thaw.* …*none* of my *lanterns* …*burn* *without* *it.*

conversations.title: Corliss — the sexton at the feast

nodes.speaker: Corliss
nodes.text: *(She stands a careful distance from the hearth, holding a cup she hasn't drunk from, surveying the preparations with a professional eye that has never once been pointed at a celebration.)* …i keep *cataloguing* it, cold one. *occupational* *disease.* …*(she nods around the room)* …the *candles:* she'd *place* them *lower*, for the *shadows.* the *bread:* *bought*, she'll *clock* it in a *heartbeat* and *love* us *anyway.* the *guests:* …*(her voice does something unexpected)* …the *guests* are *perfect.* …*(she turns to you)* …do you know what i *do*, at my *wakes?* i *speak* for souls *nobody* *came* for. i stand over the *unmarked* and i *make* the *mark* — *late*, *always* *late*, the only *mourner* a *stranger* *paid* in *nothing.* …*(she gestures at the warm, filling room)* …*this* is my *first* — in the *whole* *office*, cold one — my *first* *gathering* for a soul *everyone* came for …*while* *she's* *still* *here* to *count* *the* *house.* …*(dry, and not dry)* …i had *no* *idea* the *job* *had* this *version.* …*nobody* *told* the *sexton* …you could do the *marking* …*early.*

choices.text: *(read the sexton at her first feast)* "Let me look at you, Corliss. The wake-keeper in a warm room. I want to see what tonight is doing to the office."

*(the one who crosses — and who sat at her wakes)* "You marked the unmarked when no one else would, Corliss — I witnessed it. So hear this from the one who walks both ways: tonight IS your office. Same work, same words, one difference — the guest of honor gets to hear them. You've been rehearsing for this wake your whole death. It's just early enough, for once, to be called a feast."
"Drink the cup, Corliss. You're off-duty. That's an order from the one soul here who outranks a sexton."

nodes.speaker: Corliss
nodes.text: *(She lets you look with the flat, unbothered patience of a woman who has stood over too many truths to fear one, and your sense goes into the sexton and finds the office, and what tonight is quietly doing to it.)* *(The vocation is intact — the fierce, unpaid, load-bearing insistence that no soul go unmarked, the grief-as-guard-duty you read the first time you met her. But your sense finds it changed at the root by a single arithmetic she has been running since Marisa's invitation arrived: that every wake she has ever held was a debt paid to a soul who could no longer collect. Beautiful, necessary, and always, structurally, too late — the mark made after the marked could feel it. And tonight is the control experiment her office never permitted: the same words, the same witness, the same we-saw-you-you-mattered — delivered on time, to a face, in a warm room, while the honored can blush and deflect and be embarrassed and be HELD. And your sense reads the conclusion forming in her — sexton-precise, revolutionary in the smallest possible way: that she will not stop keeping wakes, the dead need their sexton; but that she is going to start keeping this too. She has already drafted the rule, in the same dry ledger-hand she files everything: 'Where possible, mark them living.' Three words that would have changed every grief she has ever tended. And your sense reads, at the very bottom, the private entry she will never say aloud: that somewhere in the long list of souls Corliss has marked, there is one name that has never been marked by anyone — hers — and that tonight, watching a room do for Dot what no room ever did for the sexton, she is taking notes in two ledgers at once.)*

nodes.speaker: Corliss
nodes.text: *(The reframe lands the way truth lands on the precise: audibly. You can almost hear the office reorganize itself around it.)* …*early* *enough* to be *called* a *feast.* …*(she sets the cup down, takes out the small black book she files her wakes in, and — with great deliberateness, in front of you — turns to a fresh page)* …then i'm *working* *tonight* after all. …*(the dry ghost of a smile)* …*'Dorothea* *Marigold*, of the *Marigold* *ovens.* *Fed* the *ward* that *forgot* her *god.* *Threw* the *feasts* *nobody* *else* would. *Taught* the *frozen* to *light* *lanterns* and the *doomed* to *dance.* …*Marked* — *(she writes the word slowly, savoring the tense of it)* …*living.'* …*(she closes the book)* …i'll *read* it at the *toasts.* *short.* she'll *cry.* the *sister* will cry. the *new* *girl* will *definitely* cry. …*(she picks the cup back up, and this time she drinks)* …*first* *entry* in the *new* *ledger*, cold one. …*'where* *possible* …*mark* *them* *living.'* …*(a beat)* …i intend to make *'possible'* …a much *bigger* *word* …than my *office* *ever* *let* it *be.*

nodes.speaker: Corliss
nodes.text: *(She looks at the cup, and at you, and something in the dry sexton face concedes the point with honors.)* …*outranked.* …*(she drinks — properly, not a sip — and sets the cup down with the care of a woman doing an unfamiliar rite correctly)* …*hm.* …*(almost surprised)* …it's *good.* …*(she permits herself to lean, one degree, against the warm wall)* …you know the last time i was at a gathering i wasn't *conducting*, cold one? …*(she genuinely calculates)* …*neither* do i. that's the *answer.* the *ledger* doesn't go *back* that *far.* …*(she watches the room fill — the sister, the girl, the candles, the laid table)* …*look* at them. …*amateurs.* every one. wrong *candle*-height, *bought* *bread*, *no* *order* of *service* — …*(and then, the thing under the dryness, plain for one sentence)* …and it's the *finest* *piece* of *marking* i've *ever* *stood* *in.* …*go* *on*, cold one. *mingle.* …the *sexton's* *off*-*duty.* …*(she picks the cup back up)* …*apparently* …*that's* *allowed.*

conversations.title: Renn — the guest who showed up

nodes.speaker: Renn
nodes.text: *(She finishes the cups and stands back to check her work — every one aligned, the care of someone very new taking the smallest job very seriously — and then looks up at you with the face of a soul who still can't quite believe she's included.)* …Marisa said *everyone* who *owed* her a *kindness*, and i almost didn't *come*, because i never *met* her, not *really* — but then i thought about it *properly.* …*(she counts it out, careful as the cups)* …the *feast* kept the *Quarter* warm. the *warm* *Quarter* is where the *souls* live who were *kind* to me when i was *new.* so the kindness that reached *me* had *her* *flour* on it, even if her *hands* never touched it. …*(she looks at the door, where Dot will come in)* …is that — do you think that *counts*, cold one? *secondhand* *gratitude? …showing* *up* for someone who *warmed* you *without* *knowing* it? …*(anxious, hopeful, entirely Renn)* …i don't want to take a *chair* from someone with a *better* *claim.*

choices.text: *(read the new soul at her first feast)* "Let me look at you a second, Renn. It's been a while since the stall. I want to see how keeping your name turned out."

*(the one who told her a name isn't loose change)* "It counts double, Renn. Firsthand thanks is a receipt — secondhand thanks is proof the warmth traveled. You're not taking a chair from someone with a better claim. You ARE the better claim: you're the evidence her feast worked on people she never even met. Sit at the table. Sit near the front."
"You showed up, Renn. That's the whole job of a feast. Everything else is placement of cups."

nodes.speaker: Renn
nodes.text: *(She holds still, only a little nervous now — the last time you looked at her she was clutching her name like a coal at a fraud's stall — and your sense goes in and finds what keeping it built.)* *(The grief is still there. That is the first, best finding: the quarrel never mended, the person on the far side of a hard word, the whole unfinished ache she nearly sold for a comfort — still hers, still carried, and carrying it has done exactly what the pardoner's lie never could: it has kept her a person. Your sense reads how she holds it now — not as a wound she circles but as ballast, the weight that keeps the new soul steady in the grey's currents, proof on the worst nights that she loved her life enough for it to hurt. And your sense reads what has grown around the kept name: a quiet vocation of thresholds. She remembers, in her body, what it is to stand at an edge about to trade away the last of yourself for the promise of not hurting — so she has become, in her small new way, a soul who stands at edges with people: the queue, the fires, tonight the cups. Never the loudest. Always early. Always the one who makes sure the smallest task is done with enormous care, because she knows now that the smallest things — a name, a cup set straight, a stranger who looks at your face — are the load-bearing ones. And your sense reads the simple thing at the bottom, the engine of her whole new death: she is paying it forward at one-to-one scale, kindness for kindness, cup for cup, and she has no idea — none — that this is exactly how the warmth compounds, that she is already somebody's Dot and doesn't know it. …the fever-dream of the grey is that souls dissolve. The quiet truth in this one is that they also, given half a chance, RISE.)*

nodes.speaker: Renn
nodes.text: *(She takes it in — proof the warmth traveled — and stands a little straighter over her cups.)* …*evidence.* …*(she tries the word on and it fits)* …i'm *evidence.* …*(a small, growing smile)* …then i should — if i'm *evidence*, i should *testify*, shouldn't i. at the *toasts.* …*(the old anxiety flickers and she talks herself through it, out loud, the way she's learned to)* …a *whole* *room* *looking* at me. …okay. okay, but it's a *warm* room. and the *worst* *thing* isn't being *looked* at — i *learned* that one at the *Wall's* edge, the worst thing is being *by* *yourself* *forever* — and this is the *exact* *opposite* of *by* *yourself* *forever*, this is *WITH* *everybody* *tonight* — …*(she nods, decided, and picks up the fullest cup to have it ready)* …i'll say the *secondhand* thing. the *flour* on the *kindness.* she should *know* her *feast* reached souls who never *saw* it. …*(she looks at you, bright)* …*you* keep doing this, you know. *stall*, *cups*, doesn't *matter* — you look at the *smallest* soul in the *room* …and *hand* them a *bigger* *part.* …*(fierce, delighted)* …*front* *chair.* …i'm *taking* the *front* *chair.*

nodes.speaker: Renn
nodes.text: *(She looks at her cups — every one aligned — and laughs, surprising herself.)* …*'placement* of *cups.'* …*(she straightens one that didn't need it, on purpose, grinning)* …the *lady* on the *queue* told me, when i first came through: *'the* grey is *big*, little one, *find* a *small* *thing* and *do* it *well.'* i thought she meant it like a *chore.* *keep* *busy.* *don't* *think* about the *dark.* …*(she shakes her head slowly)* …she meant *this*, didn't she. …a *feast* is just *forty* small things done with *love* at the *same* *time.* …*somebody* *lights.* *somebody* *bakes.* *somebody* *shows* *up* *early* and does the *cups.* …*(she takes her place by the table, keeper of the smallest post, entirely sure of it now)* …*Dot* *does* *all* *forty*, is the *thing.* …*tonight* she does *zero.* …*(a whisper, delighted, as the door sounds)* …*places*, cold one. …*the* *zero* *starts* *now.*
